chunks.sanskrit: vyāptacarācarabhāvaviśeṣaṃ cinmayam ekam anantam anādim bhairavanātham anāthaśaraṇyaṃ tvanmayacittatayā hṛdi vande
chunks.l1:
## bh-p01 (1)
pervading-the-particular-states-of-moving-and-unmoving / consisting-of-consciousness / one / endless / beginningless / Bhairava-Lord / of-helpless-refuge / by-mind-become-Yours / in-heart / I-venerate // bh-p01
chunks.l2: Pervading the particular states of moving and unmoving — consciousness-made, one, endless, beginningless: Bhairava-Lord, refuge of the helpless — by mind become Yours, in heart I venerate.
chunks.l3:
Pervading every state of moving and unmoving, consciousness itself is one — without end or beginning.
Bhairava, Lord, refuge of the helpless — with a mind become Yours, in my heart, I bow.
chunks.c1:
## bh-p01 — C1

**SUMMARY.** The Lord is established as all-pervading conscious reality — one, endless, beginningless — then venerated as refuge of the helpless by a mind become His.

*Rasa: śānta (tranquility) with adbhuta (wonder) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of veneration (vandana); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at consciousness pervading all. The rasa is not erotic or heroic but the tranquility of recognition beginning: the Absolute named, the devotee absorbed. Abhinava's own rasa theory (rasadhvani) is here the frame, not decoration — the verse aims at relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute, and the C1 names that relish.*
chunks.argmap:
## bh-p01 — argument map

The object is fixed in full: all-pervading (vyāpta) particular of moving-and-unmoving states (carācarabhāvaviśeṣa), consisting of consciousness (cinmaya), one (eka), endless (ananta), beginningless (anādi). The act follows: Bhairava-Lord (bhairavanātham), refuge of the helpless (anāthaśaraṇyaṃ), venerated by mind-become-Yours (tvanmayacittatayā), in heart (hṛdi) — vande (I venerate). Veneration is not ritual offering but mental absorption: the devotee's mind becoming His (tvanmaya). The name Bhairava performs its own nirukta here: bearing/supporting the universe, the Roar (rava) of AHAM, benefactor of the terrified — all three senses lived in the single act of absorption (Tantrāloka 1.95-100). Total surrender is sized to its object: the all-pervading consciousness is venerated by absorption into it, not by offering to it.

### Open
- Whether 'carācarabhāvaviśeṣa' means particular states or the particularity of states is unresolved.
- Whether 'anādi' negates temporal beginning only or all limitation is unresolved.
- The nirukta is performed, not stated; the verse does not gloss its own name.

chunks.sanskrit: tvanmayam etad aśeṣam idānīṃ bhāti mama tvadanugrahaśaktyā tvaṃ ca maheśa sadaiva mamātmā svātmamayaṃ mama tena samastam
chunks.l1:
## bh-p02 (2)
become-of-You / this / without-remainder / now / appears / to-me / by-power-of-Your-grace / You / Maheśa / always / my-self / made-of-own-self / my / through-Him / all // bh-p02
chunks.l2: All this, become of You, now appears to me by the power of Your grace. You, Maheśa, are always my self; by You all is mine.
chunks.l3:
All this, become Yours without remainder, now appears to me by the power of Your grace.
You, Maheśa, are ever my own self — made of You, all is mine through You.
chunks.c1:
## bh-p02 — C1

**SUMMARY.** Grace first discloses the world as His; then identity declared outright: Maheśa, always my self — and all mine through Him.

*Rasa: śānta (tranquility) with adbhuta (wonder) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of recognition (pratyabhijñā); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at grace disclosing the world as His. The rasa is the tranquility of non-dual identity, not the joy of acquisition — all is mine already, through Him.*
chunks.argmap:
## bh-p02 — argument map

Disclosure first: all this (etad), become of You (tvanmayam), without remainder (aśeṣam), now (idānīm) appears (bhāti) to me (mama) — by the power of Your grace (tvadanugrahaśaktyā). Then declaration: You (tvaṃ), Maheśa, always (sadaiva) my self (mamātmā); made of my own self (svātmamayaṃ), all (samastam) is mine (mama) through Him (tena). Grace is the cause of both disclosure and declaration; merit is not. Appearance, then ownership — the two-step is the pratyabhijñā structure.

### Open
- Whether 'svātmamaya' means 'made of my self' or 'self-identical' is unresolved.
- Whether 'tena' refers to grace or to Maheśa is unresolved.

chunks.sanskrit: svātmani viśvagaye tvayi nāthe tena na saṃsṛtibhītikathāsti satsv api durdharaduḥkhavimohatrāsavidhāyiṣu karmagaṇeṣu
chunks.l1:
## bh-p03 (3)
in-own-self / all-pervading / in-You / as-Lord / therefore / not / of-transmigration-fear-talk / exists / Even-though / hard-to-bear / suffering / delusion / terror / causing / in-karma-hosts // bh-p03
chunks.l2: With You as Lord, all-pervading in own self — therefore no talk of transmigration-fear. Even though hard-to-bear suffering, delusion, terror-causing karmas are present.
chunks.l3:
You, Lord, pervade my own self — so there is no talk of transmigration-fear.
Even while hard-to-bear suffering, delusion, and terror-causing karma-hosts stand.
chunks.c1:
## bh-p03 — C1

**SUMMARY.** Fear-talk denied while suffering conceded: no discussion of transmigration-fear, yet affliction stands granted — denial and concession in one breath.

*Rasa: śānta (tranquility) with karuṇa (compassion) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of fearless recognition; the vyabhicāri is concession (anukampa) of suffering without fear. The rasa is the tranquility of non-dual recognition facing suffering — not the joy of denial but the peace of no-fear.*
chunks.argmap:
## bh-p03 — argument map

Fear-talk denied: with You as Lord (nāthe) pervading (viśvagaye) own self (svātmani), therefore (tena) no talk of transmigration-fear exists (na saṃsṛtibhītikathā asti). Affliction conceded in the same breath: even though (satsvapi) hard-to-bear suffering, delusion, terror-causing karma-hosts. No-fear and full-suffering together — the concession framed by the denial, resolved within the verse, not deferred. The non-dual recognition does not deny affliction; it denies fear of it: suffering is real, fear of it is not, because there is no 'other' to fear.

### Open
- Whether 'prāyeṇa' (mostly) softens the claim or qualifies it is unresolved.
- Whether 'karmagaṇa' means masses of karma or hosts of karmic beings is unresolved.

chunks.sanskrit: antaka māṃ prati mā dṛśam enāṃ krodhakarālatamāṃ vinidhehi śaṅkarasevanacintanadhīro bhīṣaṇabhairavaśaktimayo 'smi
chunks.l1:
## bh-p04 (4)
O-Ender / toward-me / not / gaze / this / most-wrathful-terrible / direct / By-Śaṅkara-service / contemplation-firm / I-am / terrifying-Bhairava-power-filled // bh-p04
chunks.l2: O Ender, turn not toward me this most wrathful-terrible gaze. Firm in Śaṅkara-service and contemplation, I am filled with terrifying Bhairava-power.
chunks.l3:
O Ender — turn from me this most wrathful and terrible gaze.
Steadfast in Śaṅkara’s service and contemplation, I am filled with dread Bhairava-power.
chunks.c1:
## bh-p04 — C1

**SUMMARY.** Death's gaze turned aside by prayer; service and firm contemplation produce the power-filled state, testified with asmi — I am.

*Rasa: vīra (heroism) with adbhuta (wonder) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of prayer (prārthanā); the vyabhicāri is courage (dhairya) filled with Bhairava-power. The rasa is heroic, not tranquil — the devotee declares power against death's gaze. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as vīra: the sthāyibhāva of utsāha (energy) aimed at the Absolute.*
chunks.argmap:
## bh-p04 — argument map

Prayer first: O Ender (antaka), do not (mā) direct (vinidhehi) toward me (māṃ prati) this (enām) most wrathful-terrible (krodhakarālatamām) gaze (dṛśam). Then the ground: firm (dhīra) in Śaṅkara-service (sevana) and contemplation (cintana), filled (maya) with terrifying, awe-full Bhairava-power (bhīṣaṇabhairavaśakti) — asmi (I am). Power first invoked against death's gaze, then declared as state. Śaṅkara here = Śiva, not Śaṅkarācārya — the context of Bhairava-service requires it.

### Open
- Whether 'asmi' is a declaration of achieved state or a performative utterance is unresolved.
- Whether 'śaṅkara' could refer to Śaṅkarācārya is resolved as Śiva by context.

## bh-p05 (5)
thus / whose-great-darkness-is-dispelled-by-rays-of-world-awareness / Death-Yama-ender-karma-ghosts / Lord / salutation / never / I-fear // bh-p05
chunks.l2: Thus — great darkness dispelled by rays of world-awareness: death, Yama, the ender, karma-ghosts — Lord, salutation; never do I fear.
chunks.l3:
Thus — the great darkness, taken on with becoming, is dispelled by awareness’s rays:
Death, Yama, the Ender, karma-ghosts — Lord, salutation: never shall I fear.
chunks.c1:
## bh-p05 — C1

**SUMMARY.** Darkness already burned away by awareness; four terrors then met with salutation alone, yielding absolute fearlessness.

*Rasa: śānta (tranquility) with adbhuta (wonder) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of fearlessness (abhaya); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at darkness dispelled. The rasa is the tranquility of no-fear, not the thrill of confrontation — the terrors are met with salutation, not defiance.*
chunks.argmap:
## bh-p05 — argument map

Great darkness already dispelled (dārita bhūri tamisra) by rays (dīdhiti) of awareness (saṃvid) consisting of world-becoming (bhavanmaya). Then the catalogue — death, Yama, ender, karma-ghosts — met with salutation (namo 'stu) alone. Never (na jātu) fear (bibhemi): awareness burned the dark before the terrors were named. Salutation finishes what light began: the terrors are met with salutation, not weapons.

### Open
- Whether 'bhavanmaya' (world-becoming) modifies awareness or rays is unresolved.
- Whether the four terrors are a complete list or exemplary is unresolved.

chunks.sanskrit: proditasatyavibodhamarīciprekṣitaviśvapadārthasatattvaḥ bhāvaparāmṛtanirbharapūrṇe tvayi aham ātmani nirvṛtim emi
chunks.l1:
## bh-p06 (6)
whose-true-essence-of-world-objects-is-seen-by-rays-of-arisen-true-awakening / In-being-full / in-you / I / self / bliss / I-enter // bh-p06
chunks.l2: The true essence of world-objects is seen by rays of arisen true awakening. In being-full in You — I, the self, enter bliss.
chunks.l3:
True awakening has dawned — its rays reveal each thing’s true essence:
In You — brimming full of supreme nectar — I myself enter bliss.
chunks.c1:
## bh-p06 — C1

**SUMMARY.** True awakening discloses things as they are; bliss is entry into the Lord's fullness — ingress, not feeling.

*Rasa: ānanda (bliss) with adbhuta (wonder) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of entry (praveśa); the vyabhicāri is bliss (ānanda) of awakening. The rasa is bliss as ingress, not as feeling — the devotee enters what the Lord already is.*
chunks.argmap:
## bh-p06 — argument map

Arisen (prodita) true (satya) awakening (vibodha): its rays (marīci) reveal (prekṣita) the true essence (satattva) of world-objects (viśvapadārtha). On that ground — in You (tvayi), being-full (bhāvaparāmṛtanirbharapūrṇa), I the self (aham ātmani) enter (emi) bliss (nirvṛtim). Awakening discloses; entry is bliss; pūrṇa (full/complete) is the Lord's nature. Bliss is ingress into fullness, not a feeling produced.

### Open
- Whether 'prodita' (arisen) modifies awakening or rays is unresolved.
- Whether 'bhāvaparāmṛtanirbharapūrṇa' is one compound or several is unresolved.

## bh-p07 (7)
into-mind's-range / comes / when-indeed / affliction-state / producing-slight-anguish / Lord / then-alone / my / with-you-nondifference / hymn-supreme-nectar-rain / arises // bh-p07
chunks.l2: When the affliction-state, producing slight anguish, comes into the mind's range — Lord, then alone is my nondifference with You; the supreme-nectar-rain arises.
chunks.l3:
Whenever affliction, dealing slight anguish, comes within the mind’s reach —
then alone, Lord, my nondifference from You: the hymn rains supreme nectar.
chunks.c1:
## bh-p07 — C1

**SUMMARY.** Affliction's arrival is the occasion, not the obstacle: with it comes nondifference, and nectar arises.

*Rasa: śānta (tranquility) with adbhuta (wonder) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of nondifference (abheda); the vyabhicāri is joy (harṣa) that affliction is the occasion. The rasa is the tranquility of recognition in suffering — not the joy of pain but the peace that suffering is not other.*
chunks.argmap:
## bh-p07 — argument map

When indeed (yadaiva) the affliction-state (kleśadaśā), producing slight anguish (tanutāpavidhātrī), comes (eti) into the mind's range (mānasagocaram) — — then alone (tadaiva) my nondifference with You (mama tvadabhedaḥ), and the rain of supreme nectar arises (stotraparāmṛtavṛṣṭir udeti). Affliction's arrival dated as nondifference's occasion: with it, not after it, the nectar rains. The verse inverts the expected: suffering is not the enemy of recognition but its trigger.

### Open
- Whether 'tanutāpa' (slight anguish) is physical or mental is unresolved.
- Whether 'yadaiva' is temporal or conditional is unresolved.

**SUMMARY.** Rites relativized — vow, giving, bathing, austerity dispel heat — while scripture contemplated as nectar irrigates the mind with a bliss-stream.

*Rasa: śānta (tranquility) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of contemplation (cintā); the vyabhicāri is peace (śānti) of the bliss-streamed mind. The rasa is the tranquility of contemplation, not the austerity of rites.*
chunks.argmap:
## bh-p08 — argument map

Truly (satyam), O Śaṅkara: vow (vrata), giving (dāna), bathing (snāna), austerity (tapas) — dispels (vidāri) becoming's heat (bhavatāpa). Rites relativized, not despised: heat dispelled by rites. Contemplation (cintā) of Your (tāvaka) scripture (śāstra) as supreme nectar (parāmṛta), in mind (cetasi), streams (syandati) a bliss-stream (nirvṛtidhārā). Heat dispelled by rites; bliss streamed by contemplation.

chunks.argmap:
# Bhairavastava bh-p09 — ARGUMENT MAP (verse 9)

*2026-10-31. Source: T1 bh-p09 = verse 9 (restored 2026-10-31: first half nṛtyati...bhairavanātha now glossed — consciousness dances before obtaining is defined). Lore: samayajña (knower of the samaya) restricts the verse's "beautiful vision" (sudarśana) to the initiated — samaya customarily denotes the post-initiatory discipline in Trika contexts; the verse thus marks obtaining-the-Lord as an insider's vision, hard for others by structure, not by divine stinginess.*

---

## 1. What is at issue

Verse 9 of the Bhairavastava (Abhinavagupta, 10 verses). Gloss: dances (nṛtyati) [and]-sings (gāyati) [and]-rejoices (hṛṣyati) [and]-deeply (gāḍham) [and]-consciousness (saṃvit) [and]-this (iyam) [and]-my (mama) [and]-O-Bhairava-Lord (bhairavanātha) [and]-You (tvāṃ) [and]-dear (priyam) [and]-having-obtained (āpya) [and]-beautiful-vision-alone (sudarśanamekam) [and]-hard-to-get-by-others (durlabhamanyajanaiḥ) [and]-samaya-knower (samayajñam) // abhts_9

Sanskrit: nṛtyati gāyati hṛṣyati gāḍhaṃ saṃvid iyaṃ mama bhairavanātha | tvāṃ priyam āpya sudarśanamekaṃ durlabham anyajanaiḥ samayajñam

## 2. The argument, reconstructed step by step

**Verse 9:**
> nṛtyati gāyati hṛṣyati gāḍhaṃ saṃvid iyaṃ mama bhairavanātha | tvāṃ priyam āpya sudarśanamekaṃ durlabham anyajanaiḥ samayajñam

[i.e. dances, sings, deeply rejoices — this consciousness of mine, O Bhairava-Lord; having obtained You, the dear — the beautiful vision alone, hard to get by others, O knower of the samaya.]

Joy first: this consciousness of mine (saṃvid iyaṃ mama) dances (nṛtyati), sings (gāyati), deeply (gāḍham) rejoices (hṛṣyati) — O Bhairava-Lord. Then its cause named: having obtained (āpya) You, the dear (priyam) — the beautiful vision alone (sudarśanam ekam), hard to get by others (durlabham anyajanaiḥ) — O knower of the samaya (samayajña). Obtaining is defined as vision (sudarśana), and vision is fenced: the samaya-knower's portion.

## 3. Unresolved / uncertain (not invented)

1. Samaya is read in its initiatory-discipline sense; the verse itself gives no gloss — marked as reading, not fact.
2. Restored 2026-10-31: T1 previously covered only the verse's second half; the rejoicing-consciousness first half is now glossed and parsed.

## 4. Decision for L2

Carry joy-then-cause: dancing consciousness, then obtaining defined as rare vision. L2 must keep "alone" (ekaṃ) and "hard to get by others" — rarity is structural to the claim. Carry the obtained vision into verse 10, where vision acts outward as pacification.

## bh-p10 (10)
in-the-month-of-Pauṣa / on-the-dark-tenth / Abhinavagupta / hymn / this / made / By-whom / the-Lord / becomes / world's / great-heat / pacifies / instantly / compassionate // bh-p10
chunks.l2: In the month of Pauṣa, on the dark tenth, Abhinavagupta made this hymn. The pervasive, compassionate Lord pacifies the world's desert-heat — instantly.
chunks.l3:

chunks.c1:
## bh-p10 — C1

**SUMMARY.** Dated and signed, it turns outward: the compassionate Lord pacifies the world's heat instantly — what began in the heart ends in the world.

*Rasa: śānta (tranquility) with karuṇa (compassion) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of pacification (śamana); the vyabhicāri is compassion (karuṇā) of the dated hymn. The rasa is the tranquility of compassion — the hymn that began in inward dissolution ends in world-pacification.*
chunks.argmap:
## bh-p10 — argument map

In the month of Pauṣa, on the dark tenth, Abhinavagupta made this hymn: dated, signed. By whom (yena) — devotee or hymn, undivided in effect — the pervasive (vibhuḥ), compassionate (dayāluḥ) Lord becomes (bhavati), pacifies (śamayati) the world's desert-heat of becoming — instantly (jhaṭiti). The dated hymn turns outward: private recognition cools the world. The verse moves from colophon to pacification to speed: inward dissolution (v.1) to world-pacification.

### Open
- Whether 'yena' refers to devotee or hymn is unresolved.
- Whether 'bhavamarusantāpa' is physical or existential heat is unresolved.
